methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.skip_reason: insufficient narrow peer set in Chips & Semiconductors (found 0 same-stage, 1 adjacent-stage, 0 similar-tier; need ≥3)
methods.rationale: 11 same-sector peers exist in Chips & Semiconductors, but none of the narrow filters (same-stage / adjacent-stage / similar-valuation-tier) yielded ≥3 datapoints. Falling back to all-sector median would be misleading.

data.narrative:
OBSIDIA Semiconductor is a seed-stage company in the Chips & Semiconductors sector. The valuation universe consists of 11 same-sector peers—3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms, including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent. However, the peer set presents material constraints for conventional valuation triangulation.

The Peer-Median method is not applicable. Despite 11 same-sector comparables existing, filtering for same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier peers yielded fewer than three datapoints in any narrow cohort. Relying on an all-sector median would conflate seed-stage frontier semiconductor ventures with mature public chipmakers and later-stage private development firms, introducing unacceptable basis distortion. No other triangulation methods were documented as applicable against the provided data.

The analysis cannot support a specific valuation range. OBSIDIA's early stage, combined with the fragmentation of the peer universe across vastly different maturity levels and business models, prevents reliable cross-sectional benchmarking. Key uncertainties include the absence of disclosed fundraising data, the heterogeneity of the top private peers (spanning quantum computing, AI accelerators, and custom silicon), and the inherent gap between seed-stage private valuations and public market multiples. A credible valuation would require either: additional seed-stage comparables within narrower technical segments, forward-looking financial projections, or primary market intelligence on recent transaction terms within the frontier semiconductor cohort.
